newsitem.title: PERU: BellSouth to invest in Peruvian phone market.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth to invest in Peruvian phone market.

text.p: U.S. telecommunications giant BellSouth is to invest in Peru's conventional telephones market, through its Peruvian unit, Tele2000, high executives said.
"BellSouth came to Peru to become the biggest operator," told Reuters Tele2000 vice-president Rafael Diez Canseco.
"Starting June of 1999, we think we will compete with any other conventional telephones operator."
In that year, the monopoly of Telefonica del Peru, who won the 1994 privatization of the state telecommunications firm, will end.
BellSouth bought 57 percent of the shares of Tele2000 with $112.2 million in January. It currently owns 59.5 percent of the shares due to recent acquisitions.
Canseco said the commercial offensive in Peru was part of a strategy to increase its presence in Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Chile, Argentina, Uruguay, Brazil, Nicaragua and Panama.
The most recent acquisition of BellSouth was in Sao Paulo, where it bought a cellular phone concession for $2.5 billion.
Tele2000, which operates telephone services and television cables, received investments in 1995 amounting to $43.6 million, a 25 percent increase from 1995.
In the first quarter of this year, Tele2000 received an income of $13.2 million compared with $10.1 million the same time last year.
The company is valued at $180 million in the stock market.
Canseco said BellSouth would invest $150 million to increase the cellular phone net of its subsidiary.
"Our net has increased 70 to 75 percent up to date, we hope to double that by the end of the year, compared with 1996."
Tele2000 and Telefonica del Peru, a subsidiary of Telefonica de Espana, are currently disputing the terms of Telefonica del Peru's cellular phone concession.
"(Telefonica del Peru) only has monopoly for long- distance and international calls, but they do not have a monopoly of the cellular market," Canseco said.
Canseco also said the investment was planned because of strong projections for the Peruvian market.
"We are not giving numbers, but we know it is a strong growth...In May-June we beat the sales record," he said.
The government is planning to convoke the finalists for the sale of band "B" cellular concession for provincial Peru.
The sale is expected to earn $100 million and Tele2000 is strongly interested.
"We want to win. Strategically, BellSouth and Tele2000 are interested in operating in the provincial market," Canseco added.
((-- Lima newsroom, 511 221-2134))
